articles.title: Drug-resistant infections put wounded Ukrainian soldiers at risk of amputation. Doctors are trying to help by treating them like victims of a biological attack.
articles.description: In late October, The New York Times published a report on how doctors are helping Ukrainian soldiers fight antibiotic-resistant infections. Correspondent Marc Santora traveled to Dnipro and Poland, spoke with doctors and patients, and joined science reporter Gina Kolata to examine the problem and a potential solution. Here, we summarize their reporting alongside additional details from the participating doctors’ interviews, presentations, and scientific papers.

articles.title: Manipur: COCOMI Seeks Rehabilitation for 2,000 Displaced Naga People, Calls for SoO Abrogation
articles.description: IMPHAL: The Coordinating Committee on Manipur Integrity (COCOMI) has urged the Central and State Government to take immediate steps to rehabilitate internally displaced persons (IDPs) from the Naga community, alleging that around 2,000 people, including women and children, have been displaced by a series of attacks allegedly carried out by Kuki militants in Ukhrul and Kamjong districts. Speaking to Organiser Weekly at the COCOMI office in Imphal on Sunday, COCOMI spokesperson Mayengbam Dhananjoy Singh condemned the reecnt attacks on Naga communities and expressed concern over the plight of those forced to flee their homes. He said the displaced people are currently taking shelter in Imphal and surrounding areas, largely in the houses of relatives and acquaintances, as the government has not established separate relief camps for them. Read More: Noney gunfight leaves three dead in Manipur; Civilian convoy comes under attack in Litan According to the Spokesperson of COCOMI, since these displaced people have not been formally recognised as internally displaced persons, they have been deprived of the humanitarian assistance and other benefits extended to IDPs residing in designated relief camps across the hill and valley districts. Raising concerns over their livelihood and immediate survival, he questioned how displaced families could sustain themselves in unfamiliar locations without employment or any regular source of income, particularly when they are dependent on relatives and friends for shelter. He maintained that the Naga community members displaced by the recent attacks are equally victims of the ongoing conflict in Manipur and deserve the same humanitarian assistance and rehabilitation measures extended to other displaced families. Reiterating COCOMI’s long-standing demands, he called for the rehabilitation and resettlement of all internally displaced persons and the abrogation of the Suspension of Operations (SoO) agreement with Kuki militant groups. He alleged that the government was effectively allowing Kuki militant groups operating under the SoO framework to enjoy immunity despite their alleged involvement in series of violence. He asserted that if the government was genuinely committed to restoring peace in Manipur, “it must demonstrate the political will to abrogate the SoO agreement and undertake a sincere and inclusive rehabilitation process for all displaced communities.”

articles.title: Manipur government releases Rs. 5.88 crore as festival relief for 58,863 IDPs
articles.description: The Government of Manipur released Rs. 5,88,63,000 to assist 58,863 Internally Displaced Persons for festive celebrations. This financial assistance amounts to Rs. 1,000 per eligible individual and was transferred through Direct Benefit Transfer. The funds were allocated to Deputy Commissioners in ten districts for timely distribution after verification. Yumnam Khemchand Singh expressed gratitude for the government's efforts and extended Diwali greetings to citizens.
